title: UKPNP High Level Delegation Briefs British MPs on Kashmir Crisis and Current Situation in the State of Jammu Kashmir in London House of Parliament
excerpt: A high level UKPNP delegation led by Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri briefed British MPs in the House of Parliament on the Kashmir crisis, historical context, and current developments.
author: Special Correspondent, London UK

heroImage.caption: UKPNP delegation briefing British MPs at the House of Parliament.

body.text: A high level delegation of the United Kashmir People’s National Party met and briefed British MPs Fabian Hamilton, Richard Burgon, Imran Hussain and others at the House of Parliament.
The delegation included senior UKPNP leadership from Europe and the UK.
Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri explained the historical foundation of the State of Jammu and Kashmir and the root causes of its forced division.
He reaffirmed that the Kashmir conflict is not a religious, territorial, or bilateral dispute.
The delegation outlined the events of 1947, the invasion by Pakistan, and the provisional accession to India.
They discussed UN resolutions, Pakistan’s actions in Gilgit Baltistan and Azad Kashmir, and decades of restrictions on political rights.
The delegation highlighted recent blackouts, killings of peaceful protesters, and widespread communication shutdowns.
They described UKPNP’s diplomatic efforts at the United Nations and in the diaspora.
Fabian Hamilton MP reaffirmed support for the right to self‑determination and the need for peaceful resolution.
The delegation emphasized that there is no military solution and that fundamental rights must be respected.
